title: NSIDC-0666
abstract: This data set contains data obtained by the Passive Active L- and S-band (PALS) microwave aircraft instrument that are matched up with a variety of soil moisture campaign data. The data were collected as part of four different campaigns: Southern Great Plains 1999 (SGP99), Cloud and Land Surface Interaction Campaign 2007 (CLASIC07), Soil Moisture Experiment 2002 (SMEX02), and the SMAP Validation Experiment 2008 (SMAPVEX08).

title: AirMOSS_L4_RZ_Soil_Moisture_1421
abstract: This dataset offers 1 hours gridded soil moisture estimates derived from hydrologic modeling at nine AirMOSS sites across North America. The AirMOSS L4 RZSM product temporally interpolates the intermittent AirMOSS L2/3 RZSM retrievals into a continuous, multi-layer, 1 hours soil moisture dataset. The L4 RZSM data maintain the same spatial resolution (3-arcseconds or approximately 100 meters) and temporal coverage (generally from Fall 2012 through Fall 2015) as the L2/3 RZSM data. The L4 RZSM data were generated by integrating the Level 2/3 product with other ancillary information into the Penn State Integrated Hydrologic Model (PIHM). These temporally continuous RZSM estimates are crucial for many key applications of AirMOSS data products, such as calculating net ecosystem exchange (NEE).

title: ND30_REE_WATER_ CHEMISTRY_1131
abstract: Airborne soil moisture measurement relies on the variation in natural terrestrial gamma radiation flux observed between wet and dry soils. When soil contains moisture, its density effectively increases, leading to greater attenuation of gamma flux in wetter soils and a consequently lower flux at the surface. During the FIFE experiment, natural terrestrial gamma radiation data were collected across a network of 24 flight lines. The data acquisition process was designed to gather and store spectral radiation data along these flight lines, from which soil moisture estimates could be derived. A one-time calibration of the natural terrestrial radioisotope signal was performed using ground-based soil moisture measurements over the flight line network. A time-series of airborne soil moisture measurements (to a depth of 20 cm) was then compared to a comprehensive, independent data set of ground-based soil moisture measurements. The estimates for flight line segments exhibited an average RMS error of approximately 2.5% soil moisture (Peck et al., 1990).

title: ABoVE_PBand_SAR _1657
abstract: This dataset contains estimates of soil geophysical properties derived from Airborne Microwave Observatory of Subcanopy and Subsurface (AirMOSS) P-band polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data collected during August and October of 2014, 2015, and 2017 over 12 study sites in Northern Alaska. The reported soil properties include active layer thickness (ALT), dielectric constant, soil moisture profile, surface roughness, and their respective uncertainty estimates, all provided at a 30-meter spatial resolution across the 12 flight transects. Most study sites are within the continuous permafrost zone, where the minimal aboveground vegetation, primarily dwarf shrubs and tussock/sedge/moss tundra, has little impact on P-band radar backscatter.

title: ABoVE_ReSALT_InSAR _PolSAR_V3_2004
abstract: This dataset offers estimates of seasonal subsidence, active layer thickness (ALT), vertical soil moisture profiles, and associated uncertainties at a 30-meter resolution for 51 sites across the ABoVE domain, which includes 39 sites in Alaska and 12 in Northwest Canada. The ALT and soil moisture profile estimates were derived using L- and P-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data collected by the NASA/JPL Uninhabited Aerial Vehicle Synthetic Aperture Radar (UAVSAR) instruments during the 2017 Arctic Boreal Vulnerability Experiment (ABoVE) airborne campaign. The data are available in NetCDF Version 4 format and include a Python script for estimating soil volumetric water content from the provided data.

title: BOREAS_H6ACGSMD _270
abstract: This dataset includes measurements of soil moisture content (by weight) and water content (if there is a moss/humus layer) obtained using a terrestrial gamma ray instrument from an aircraft. It also contains data indicating the aircraft's location at the time of data collection, with coordinates detailing the flight paths for various lines and bins. The data were collected during four periods from September 1993 to September 1994 over the Southern Study Area (SSA) and two periods from February to August 1994 over the Northern Study Area (NSA). The data are provided in tabular ASCII files.

title: AirMOSS_L2_3_RZ_ Soil_Moisture_1418
abstract: This dataset provides Level 2/3 root zone soil moisture (RZSM) estimates at multiple depths with a 90-meter spatial resolution, derived from the Airborne Microwave Observatory of Subcanopy and Subsurface (AirMOSS) radar instrument. Data were collected over ten sites across North America using a P-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) flown on a NASA Gulfstream-III aircraft. These soil moisture estimates reflect the effects of soil, topography, and vegetation heterogeneity over areas approximately 100 km by 25 km at each study site. AirMOSS flight campaigns were conducted at least biannually from 2012 to 2015 at each site.
